title: Understand the customer before choosing the build
outcome: Turn observed customer work into a bounded project brief.
story: Amina asks for “an AI that runs the shop.” You need to find the actual problem, agree on a useful first outcome, and explain which work belongs in a later release.

frames.explanation: An observed workflow makes the problem testable.

values.label: scope
values.value: Policy answers with citations and staff fallback

frames.explanation: A small agreement clarifies what success means and what remains manual.

sections.title: Observe before proposing
paragraphs: Ask the customer to show the current task with safe sample data. Who does it, how often, what takes time, and what happens when it goes wrong? Listen for constraints such as unreliable connectivity, staff skills, privacy, and systems already in use.

An FDE works close to the customer, translates the need into software, and follows the result in use. This includes communication, data integration, debugging, deployment, and handoff. Choosing a model is only one implementation decision.

sections.title: Define an outcome and a baseline
paragraphs: An outcome describes a change for the customer: reduce median reply preparation time while maintaining supported answers. Measure the current workflow before setting a target. Define who reviews correctness and how ambiguous cases are handled.
Separate the desired outcome from a feature. “Use AI” is an implementation preference, not a success measure. A search page might solve the problem with less risk; compare that alternative honestly.

sections.title: Set scope and acceptance together
paragraphs: List must-have and later features. For each must-have, write a measurable acceptance condition, expected failure behaviour, and responsible reviewer. Include access rules, operations, and support work in the scope.

The exercise filters a prepared requirements list. It does not perform discovery or judge whether a stated requirement is truly necessary. The project requires an actual conversation or an explicitly labelled role-play, observations, and a customer-reviewed brief.

sections.title: Make tradeoffs visible
paragraphs: Document assumptions, dependencies, data access, risks, and open questions. State what the first release excludes and why. Record who can approve a scope change and how it affects cost and delivery.

Demonstrate a small working slice early using real customer constraints and safe data. Capture feedback and change the brief when evidence changes. A clear disagreement explained with evidence is more useful than silently building an unrealistic promise.

exercise.title: A bounded first-release list
exercise.brief: Write scope(requirements). Keep tasks labelled necessary and measurable with true booleans. Trim non-empty task names, remove duplicates, and keep at most three in their original order.

steps.title: Keep required work
steps.task: Select necessary tasks and return their names.
steps.hint: filter chooses records; map chooses their task fields.

steps.title: Require measurable acceptance
steps.task: Keep only records whose necessary and measurable flags are true.
steps.hint: Check both flags before selecting a task.

steps.title: Normalize and bound the list
steps.task: Require strict boolean flags and string task names. Trim, remove blank/duplicate names, and limit to three.
steps.hint: Use a Set after normalizing names.

cases.label: A required task and a later task
cases.why: First release focuses on required work.

cases.why: A measurable requirement can enter scope.

cases.why: Labels must obey the agreed shape.

project.title: A customer-reviewed brief
project.brief: Interview a shop owner or conduct a clearly labelled role-play. Produce a first-release brief backed by observed tasks and measurable acceptance.
deliverables: A bounded brief with assumptions and exclusions.

milestones.title: Learn the current work
actions: Ask for a demonstration with safe examples.
Record users, volume, errors, and constraints.

milestones.title: Write the agreement
actions: Write measurable acceptance and failure behaviour.

milestones.title: Review with the customer
actions: Revise scope and identify the acceptance reviewer.

acceptance: The outcome has a baseline and measurement plan.

tests.expected: Risk and approval requirements are discussed before scope expands.
